subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Force and Torque Sensors
description: One-minute skill: Force and Torque Sensors.

hook.text: A robot inserts a peg into a hole. Without force sensing, it jams. With it, the robot feels resistance and adjusts.

buildup.text: A force-torque sensor mounts between the wrist and the tool. It measures push, pull, and twist in all six directions.

discovery.text: Strain gauges inside the sensor bend under load. The tiny deformation converts to an electrical signal proportional to force.

twist.text: Force control lets robots polish, deburr, and sand surfaces with consistent pressure. Too hard scratches. Too light misses spots.

climax.text: Surgical robots use force feedback to let surgeons feel tissue resistance through their controls. Sensing saves lives.

punchline.text: A robot that feels is a robot that adapts.

quiz.question: How do force-torque sensors help robots perform assembly tasks?
options: They increase the robot's speed so parts snap together faster
They detect resistance and allow the robot to adjust force and position to avoid jamming
They heat the parts so they expand slightly for easier insertion
